skill.name: clinvar-database
skill.description: Query NCBI ClinVar for variant clinical significance, genomic variant records, E-utilities access, bulk data formats, and VCF annotation workflows.
skill.summary: Use ClinVar references to search, interpret, and annotate human genetic variants.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily Markdown documentation for querying NCBI ClinVar and does not contain executable source code. Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown examples, official NCBI URLs, placeholder API-key text, and public data download references. One installer command is confirmed because it pipes an FTP-fetched script directly into sh.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is executed directly from an FTP download.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the sh pipe installer with official package-manager instructions, HTTPS downloads, checksum verification, and a manual review step before execution.

remediation.issue: Bulk download examples use FTP without integrity guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS endpoints where available and document checksum or signature verification for downloaded ClinVar files.

remediation.issue: Network and shell examples could be run without user confirmation by an agent.
remediation.suggestion: State that API calls, FTP downloads, and shell commands require explicit user approval before execution.

content.value_statement: ClinVar data is complex to search, interpret, and connect to genomic workflows. This skill gives structured guidance for ClinVar queries, clinical significance review, file formats, and annotation planning.
actual_capabilities: Search ClinVar by gene, condition, clinical significance, variant name, chromosome, and combined query terms.
Explain pathogenicity classes, review status stars, conflicts, and limits of VUS interpretation.
Guide E-utilities usage for esearch, esummary, efetch, and elink workflows.
Compare XML, VCF, and tab-delimited ClinVar formats for different analysis needs.
Outline VCF annotation, filtering, and bulk download workflows for bioinformatics pipelines.
Highlight release dates, genome builds, rate limits, and data quality checks for reproducible analysis.
limitations: It does not replace a clinical genetics professional or provide a medical diagnosis.
Live queries and downloads require network access and must follow NCBI rate limits.
Bulk XML and VCF files can be large and need local bioinformatics tools.
ClinVar classifications can change, so users must verify the current release before important decisions.

use_cases.title: Review a Clinical Variant
use_cases.description: Check ClinVar classifications, review status, conflicts, and evidence quality for a specific patient-relevant variant.

use_cases.title: Build an Annotation Pipeline
use_cases.description: Plan how to download ClinVar VCF files, match genome builds, annotate variants, and filter results.

use_cases.title: Study Variant Sets
use_cases.description: Search variants by disease, gene set, or pathogenicity class and compare data formats for research analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find Variants by Gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClinVar skill to help me find pathogenic variants for [GENE]. Explain the best search terms and what fields I should review first.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret a ClinVar Result
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ClinVar variant record summary: [PASTE SUMMARY]. Explain the clinical significance, review status, conflicts, and caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Plan VCF Annotation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a ClinVar annotation workflow for my VCF files on [GRCh37 or GRCh38]. Include file choice, filtering strategy, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Local ClinVar Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a reproducible local ClinVar database update process. Cover source files, schema priorities, indexing, version tracking, and validation steps.

output: Recommended query: CFTR gene plus pathogenic clinical significance and expert review status.
Review fields: clinical significance, review status, condition name, submission date, and conflicting interpretations.
Caution: confirm genome build and current ClinVar release before using results.

output_examples.input: Choose a ClinVar file format for a pipeline.
output: Use VCF for coordinate-based annotation of sequencing calls.
Use XML when full submission evidence and variant-condition details are required.
Use tab-delimited files for quick summaries, spreadsheets, or lightweight database loads.

output_examples.input: Explain a variant with conflicting interpretations.
output_examples.output: The result should be treated as unresolved until evidence is reviewed. Give more weight to expert panel or practice guideline assertions, compare submission dates, and document the conflict.

best_practices: Record the ClinVar release date, access date, genome build, and query terms for every analysis.
Prioritize expert panel and practice guideline assertions when classifications conflict.
Use caching, batch requests, and backoff to respect NCBI service limits.
anti_patterns: Treating a VUS or low-review classification as a clinical diagnosis.
Mixing GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates in the same annotation workflow.
Running remote installers or bulk download commands without verification and user approval.

faq.question: Can this skill diagnose genetic disease?
faq.answer: No. It helps interpret ClinVar data, but clinical decisions require qualified genetics professionals.

faq.question: Which ClinVar format should I use for VCF annotation?
faq.answer: Use the ClinVar VCF that matches your genome build, then validate that key variants are represented.

faq.question: Why does review status matter?
faq.answer: Review status shows evidence quality and submitter agreement. Higher star ratings usually deserve more weight.

faq.question: Can classifications change over time?
faq.answer: Yes. New evidence can change clinical significance, so important variants should be rechecked periodically.

faq.question: Does the skill require an API key?
faq.answer: An API key is optional for higher NCBI rate limits. Basic E-utilities queries can run without one.

faq.question: Is bulk ClinVar data suitable for large pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes, but users must plan for large files, update schedules, genome builds, and data validation.
